- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The play "Death of a Salesman" explores themes such as the American Dream, aging and mortality, family relationships, betrayal, and reality vs. illusion through dialogue.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Willy Loman is obsessed with achieving financial success and providing for his family, which he uses to measure his worth.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The play highlights the harsh reality of aging for Willy and Linda, discussing their fears about growing old and dying.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The dialogue centers around the Loman family and their complex relationships, including dynamics between fathers and sons, husbands and wives, and brothers.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The theme of betrayal is central to the plot, with Willy feeling betrayed by his sons, employer, and dreams.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Characters struggle to distinguish between reality and illusion, with Willy retreating into fantasy and delusion.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Willy Loman is a tragic figure representing the struggles and limitations of the American Dream, ultimately failing to achieve his goals.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Willy's desperation and disillusionment are heartbreaking, and his inability to face reality exacerbates his problems.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] Willy's character serves as a cautionary tale about the dangers of emphasizing material success over personal relationships and self-awareness.
- [ASSISTANT_SAID] The play prompts the audience to reflect on their own values and priorities, and the role of society and culture in shaping aspirations.
